findings.detail: WindowsJob.__init__ ignores the return values from TerminateProcess and the fixed 1000 ms WaitForSingleObject, then closes the process handle. Its constructor receives no remaining finalization deadline. If it raises, supervise has no job handle and retains exited=True, so its finally can delete scratch without an independently confirmed process exit. This does not meet the explicit terminate/wait and no-cleanup-before-confirmed-exit contract.
